title: region-aware-routing-economics-spot-vs-reserved-wip
summary: Working draft of cost/economics analysis for smart routing policies that blend spot, reserved/on-demand, and regional failover. Focused on per-token cost sensitivity to preemption, cross-region egress, and fallback probabilities; includes spreadsheet-style scenarios and short recommendation checklist.
body:
Background:
This doc is a working analysis to quantify tradeoffs when routing requests across: local dedicated pool (reserved or on-demand), spot/interruptible capacity, and cross-region fallback. Goal: produce a compact set of knobs for the routing policy engine (max-spot-share, regional-fallback-threshold, preemption-tolerance-ms) and an accompanying spreadsheet that product and SREs can iterate on.

Key assumptions (configurable in the spreadsheet):
- baseline token cost on on-demand GPU (us-west-2): $0.00045 / token-equivalent (normed to our batching model).
- reserved commit discount: 30% off on-demand (effective $0.000315/token).
- spot discount: 60% off on-demand median (effective $0.00018/token), but with preemption probability p_preempt varying by region and instance type.
- cross-region egress: $0.010 / GB (approx), normalized to $0.00001 / token for typical token size; higher for high-context workloads.
- latency penalty cost: assign dollar-equivalent for missed SLO (SLO_penalty_per_violation = $1.50 per 95th-pct violation event) useful to compare SLO risk vs cost savings.

Simple scenario table (per 1M tokens served) - NOTE: this is illustrative, expand in spreadsheet:

Scenario | Spot share | p_preempt | Expected tokens lost | Extra reroute tokens | Cost spot | Cost fallback | SLO risk cost | Total cost
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A: conservative | 10% | 0.02 | 2000 | 2000 | $180 | $126 | $15 | $321
B: balanced     | 40% | 0.05 | 20000 | 20000 | $720 | $1260 | $75 | $2055
C: aggressive   | 80% | 0.12 | 96000 | 96000 | $1440 | $6048 | $360 | $7848

How numbers computed (quick formulas used in the sheet):
- cost_spot = tokens_spot * spot_unit_cost
- expected_tokens_lost = tokens_spot * p_preempt
- cost_fallback = expected_tokens_lost * fallback_unit_cost (fallback unit often on-demand or reserved depending on policy)
- total_cost = cost_spot + (cost_fallback * (1 + egress_factor_if_cross_region)) + sloa_cost_estimate

Observations from quick sims:
- Spot gives large nominal savings but cost of preemption scales badly for high-context/large-kv-cache workloads because re-computation isn't cheap. For generative requests with long contexts, treat preemption cost as 2x token cost because of recompute+latency violation ripple.
- Cross-region fallback adds both egress cost and additional tail-latency risk; small egress charges can be dominated by increased SLO-violation dollar equivalents when tail percentile spikes.
- For throughput-bound workloads (high tokens/sec, batched), the system can absorb more spot capacity because recompute per-request is amortized across batch; for latency-sensitive low-batch requests prefer reserved/on-demand.

Policy knobs to expose in the routing engine (proposal):
- max_spot_share_by_route: fraction 0-1 (default 0.35 for general routes, 0.10 for low-latency routes)
- preemption_tolerance_ms: max extra ms we accept before fallback is considered a failure (default 120 ms)
- fallback_chain: ordered list [regional_reserve, regional_on_demand, cross_region_reserve, cross_region_on_demand]
- region_bias_scores: small penalties to avoid cross-region unless queue depth or latency exceed thresholds
- spot_retry_budget: per minute budget of requests that can be retried to spot after a preemption (protects from hot loops)

Mini spreadsheet snapshots to copy into master sheet (columns as CSV lines):
route_type, expected_qps, typical_context_tokens, preferred_latency_ms, default_max_spot
chat-low-latency, 20, 512, 120, 0.10
batch-embeddings, 250, 64, 1000, 0.60
interactive-tool, 80, 1024, 300, 0.25

Edge cases identified / TODOs:
- cold-starts for model shards when falling back to a region that hasn't cached KV: huge tail latency and cost of reloading weights; need a hot-standby metric and include model-shard residency probability into cost calc.
- multi-model workflows: some pipelines run several model calls; preemption in earlier calls cascades costs. Build scenario that multiplies recompute cost by pipeline length.
- spot price volatility: historical analysis by region to compute p_preempt and expected spot-run-length distributions. We should add 6 months of spot preemption telemetry and correlate with calendar events.
- run a small A/B in us-west-2: route 30% of requests for a low-risk route to spot with a 2x retry budget for 2 weeks, capture token-level costs and SLO violations.

Quick recommended defaults (starter):
- default max_spot_share = 0.35 for routes not explicitly low-latency
- route-level override for routes with expected_context_tokens > 2048 => default max_spot_share = 0.10
- cross-region fallback only allowed after regional capacity exhausted for >= 10s and queue depth > 50
- spot_retry_budget = 3 per minute per route

Action items (owners suggested):
- Asha: build canonical spreadsheet with scenario generator and parameterized formulas (sheet id draft linked above). Target: 2026-02-28 for initial sims.
- Liam: extract 6 months of spot preemption telemetry by region, instance type. Dataset: S3 path redwood-inference/telemetry/spot-preempt/2025-*.csv. Due: 2026-02-21.
- Marisol: prototype routing policy flags in staging to accept max_spot_share and spot_retry_budget. PR: routing-service#92. Due: 2026-03-07.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a working doc, numbers are intentionally rough. The main purpose is to converge on the routing knobs and attach measured preemption/egress/slack metrics instead of gut assumptions.
- When reviewing, please call out any missing cost dimension (e.g., KMS/HSM costs for private deployments, additional network tax for private VPC egress) and any constraints from Dedicated customers who require strict zero-cross-region policies.

Appendix: quick math example (detailed):
- Baseline: 1M tokens total, route uses 40% spot => tokens_spot = 400k.
- p_preempt = 0.05 => expected_lost = 20k tokens. If fallback cost uses on-demand unit cost $0.00045/token, fallback nominal cost = 20k * 0.00045 = $9.00. Spot cost = 400k * 0.00018 = $72.00. Total raw = $81.00 plus SLO risk. If SLO risk estimated at 0.5% violations at $1.50 each => 5000 * 0.005? (note: convert to event count properly in sheet).

Contact and context: this sits under product/optimize workstream to produce guidance for routing-engine and SREs. We will iterate the spreadsheet and link the canonical sheet here once first pass is uploaded.

END OF DRAFT
